text: In a republic nothing should be left to be effected by irregular methods, because, although for the time the irregularity may be useful, the example will nevertheless be pernicious, as giving rise to a practice of violating the laws for good ends, under colour of which they may afterwards be violated for ends which are not good.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
reference: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
